subject: geography
title: Drainage Basin: Stores Fill in Sequence, the River Lags

slides.heading: Drainage Basin: Stores Fill in Sequence, the River Lags
bullets: How one storm pulse is delayed by the basin stores: interception fills first and spills, the soil store fills next, percolation feeds groundwater last, overland flow switches on only at soil saturation, so the river peaks after the rain eases and recedes slowly on baseflow
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we follow one storm pulse across one drainage basin and watch the stores fill in sequence, so the river answers late.

slides.heading: What we will learn
bullets: Describe the store sequence in order: interception fills first, the soil store fills next, percolation feeds the groundwater store last
Explain why discharge peaks after the peak rain and why the recession is slow
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud and tell the class: by the end you will be able to trace one pulse of rain through the basin and explain the lag on the hydrograph.

slides.heading: The rain is heaviest at noon - so why does the river peak later?
bullets: Rain falls on the whole basin at once, yet the channel barely responds at first
If the rain does not run straight into the river, where does it wait on the way?
slides.notes: Ask the class: if the river peaked with the rain, what would the hydrograph look like? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because the water is being stored on the way.

slides.heading: Stores fill in sequence - the river answers last
bullets: Interception catches the first rain and only spills once full; the spill infiltrates and fills the soil store next
Slow percolation feeds the groundwater store last, and overland flow only switches on once the soil saturates
Discharge therefore peaks after the peak rain, then recedes slowly, sustained by groundwater baseflow
slides.notes: Stress the deciding idea: the basin is a chain of stores that must fill in sequence, and the channel only receives fast flow once the soil store is full.

slides.heading: The storm arrives and interception fills first
bullets: The storm pulse arrives, but the interception store catches the rain first and only begins to spill once it is full
The channel and the hydrograph stay flat while the first store fills
slides.notes: Play scene 1 and point to the interception store: the rain is already falling, yet the river has not responded, because the first store is still filling.

slides.heading: Soil fills next and groundwater starts last
bullets: The full interception store spills, the spill infiltrates, and the soil store fills next
Slow percolation only now starts feeding the groundwater store - still with very little flow reaching the channel
slides.notes: Play scene 2 and follow the spill downwards: the sequence is interception, then soil, then groundwater, and the channel still waits.

slides.heading: Soil saturates, overland flow peaks the river late
bullets: Once the soil store saturates, overland flow switches on and runs over the surface to the channel
Discharge rises fast and peaks now - after the rain itself has already eased and shrunk
slides.notes: Play scene 3 and compare the rain with the hydrograph: the peak discharge arrives after the peak rain, and the gap between them is the lag.

slides.heading: Rain gone, the river recedes slowly on baseflow
bullets: The rain has gone and the surface stores drain, but the hydrograph recedes only slowly
Groundwater baseflow sustains the recession, so the river falls far more slowly than it rose
slides.notes: Play scene 4 and watch the slow fall: the groundwater store, filled last, now empties last and keeps the river flowing.

slides.heading: Worked example: tracing one storm pulse
bullets: First the interception store fills and spills; then the soil store fills by infiltration; percolation feeds groundwater last
The soil saturates, overland flow switches on, and discharge peaks after the rain eases; then baseflow sustains a slow recession
slides.notes: Work it slowly: Step 1, name the store that fills first - interception. Step 2, name the store that fills next - soil. Step 3, state what switches on at saturation - overland flow. Step 4, explain the lag: the peak comes after the rain because the stores had to fill first.

slides.heading: Your turn: explain the lag
bullets: In pairs: explain to your partner why the river peaks after the heaviest rain, naming every store in sequence
Then swap and check: did your partner let any rain run straight off the surface into the river before the soil saturated?
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes. Listen for the full sequence, then take two pairs answers: interception, soil, groundwater; overland flow only at saturation; peak after the rain; slow baseflow recession.

slides.heading: Exit ticket: prove it before you leave
bullets: Your exit ticket asks you to correct a student who says the river peaks when the rain is heaviest
Name the store sequence and the moment overland flow switches on to earn full credit
slides.notes: Point to the exit ticket and remind the class: the strongest answers trace the pulse store by store and end with the baseflow recession.
